messages.author: fa9b875eb829edc8
messages.subject: Speed overestimates from camera traps
parts:
Hey Chris,

I have gotten CTMM to run on a test deployment for individuals with at least 12 points. Everything has been working well and I have been getting accurate speed measurements. However, when I run my code on all of my cameras and thus every individual my speed estimates for deer are 400 kilometers a day. Am I missing something in the code (colored in red to help) to make it overestimate? Could dt.max be the issue? When I run them individually, there are a multiple outliers with really large speeds.

Thank you!

Code: 
library(ctmm)
library(dplyr)
#install.packages("raster")
#install.packages("move")
library(move)
#library(move2)
library(readr)
library(purrr)
#most individuals have less than 10 points (?)


##SETUP##
# Load the data
data <- read.csv("merged_results.csv", header = TRUE)

# Identify sequences with any detection_idx > 0 and exclude them
sequences_to_exclude <- data %>%
  filter(detection_idx > 0) %>%
  distinct(sequence_id) %>%
  pull(sequence_id)  # Creates a vector of sequence_ids to exclude

# Filter the dataset for White-tailed Deer, excluding the identified sequences
filtered_data <- data %>%
  mutate(time = as.POSIXct(timestamp, format = "%m/%d/%y %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC")) %>%
  filter(common_name == "White-tailed Deer",
         !sequence_id %in% sequences_to_exclude,
         !duplicated(paste0(deployment_id, timestamp))) %>%
  arrange(deployment_id, time) %>%
  rename(id = transect_id, x = world_x, y = world_z)

filtered_data_oneCam <- filtered_data %>%
  filter(deployment_id == filtered_data$deployment_id[[100]])
###### 1CAMS ####
move_obj <- move(x = filtered_data_oneCam$x,
                 y = filtered_data_oneCam$y,
                 time = filtered_data_oneCam$time,
                 proj = "+proj=utm +zone=33 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +north",
                 animal = filtered_data_oneCam$sequence_id)
###### TOTAL
move_obj <- move(x = filtered_data$x,
                 y = filtered_data$y,
                 time = filtered_data$time,
                 proj = "+proj=utm +zone=33 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +north",
                 animal = filtered_data$sequence_id)

# Create a telemetry object using 'transect_id' as the individual identifier
# Here, we use direct column access rather than creating a new 'time' column unnecessarily
telemetry_data <- as.telemetry(move_obj)
 
# Display the head of the telemetry data to verify
summary(telemetry_data)

###TESTING###
i = 4 #from sequences to the whole camera as an individual animal = "how deer are using the place right in front of the camera", estimate error for the whole grid (WI, find 20 times where deer not moving - avg poosition of points is true position then look at pathagoerm theroem fistance from average point)

GUESS <- ctmm.guess(telemetry_data[[i]], CTMM=ctmm(error=1.19), interactive=FALSE)
FIT   <- ctmm.select(telemetry_data[[i]], verbose=TRUE, GUESS)
#summary(FIT [[1]])
out <- ctmm::speed(FIT[[1]], data = telemetry_data[[i]], dt.max = 600, robust = TRUE) #instantaneous speed from MM, km/day
# outs <- ctmm::speeds(FIT[[1]], data = telemetry_data[[i]], dt.max = 600, robust = TRUE) #speeds at any given location or timestep

###RUNNING###
# Create an empty list to store results
speed_results <- list()

# Loop over each individual in telemetry_data
for (i in seq_along(telemetry_data)) {
 
  # Check if the individual has enough data points (12 or 13)
  if (nrow(telemetry_data[[i]]) < 12) {  # Set to 12 or 13 based on preference
    message(paste("Skipping individual", i, "due to insufficient data points"))
    next
  }
 
  # Run ctmm.guess and ctmm.select, with error handling
  GUESS <- try(ctmm.guess(telemetry_data[[i]], CTMM = ctmm(error = 1.19), interactive = FALSE), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(GUESS, "try-error")) {
    message(paste("Error in GUESS for individual", i, "- skipping"))
    next
  }
 
  FIT <- try(ctmm.select(telemetry_data[[i]], verbose = TRUE, GUESS), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(FIT, "try-error")) {
    message(paste("Error in FIT for individual", i, "- skipping"))
    next
  }
 
  # Estimate speed, with error handling
  out <- try(ctmm::speed(FIT[[1]], data = telemetry_data[[i]], dt.max = 600, robust = TRUE), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(out, "try-error")) {
    message(paste("Error in speed estimation for individual", i, "- skipping"))
    next
  }
 
  # Store the result
  speed_results[[i]] <- out
  message(paste("Completed speed estimation for individual", i))
}

### RESULTS  # The speed_results list will contain results for each individual with sufficient data
head(speed_results)
# Loop through each result in speed_results and print the individual speed estimates and confidence intervals
for (i in seq_along(speed_results)) {
  result <- speed_results[[i]]
 
  if (!is.null(result) && "CI" %in% names(result)) {
    cat("Individual", i, "Speed Estimate: ")
    print(result$CI)  # Display the estimate and confidence interval for speed (km/day)
    cat(" ")
  } else {
    cat("Individual", i, "has no valid speed result. ")
  }
}

###ANSWERS###

# Initialize vectors to store speed estimates and confidence intervals
estimates <- c()
low_CI <- c()
high_CI <- c()

# Loop through speed_results to extract the estimates and confidence intervals
for (result in speed_results) {
  if (!is.null(result) && "CI" %in% names(result) &&
      "speed (kilometers/day)" %in% rownames(result$CI) &&
      all(c("est", "low", "high") %in% colnames(result$CI))) {
   
    # Extract the "speed (kilometers/day)" row for low, est, and high
    estimates <- c(estimates, result$CI["speed (kilometers/day)", "est"])
    low_CI <- c(low_CI, result$CI["speed (kilometers/day)", "low"])
    high_CI <- c(high_CI, result$CI["speed (kilometers/day)", "high"])
   
  } else {
    message("Skipping an entry in speed_results due to missing CI data")
  }
}

# Now you can proceed to calculate the average and CI for the extracted estimates
if (length(estimates) > 0) {
  mean_speed <- mean(estimates)
  overall_low_CI <- mean(low_CI)
  overall_high_CI <- mean(high_CI)
 
  # Calculate the standard error and rigorous CI
  std_error <- sd(estimates) / sqrt(length(estimates))
  ci_lower <- mean_speed - 1.96 * std_error
  ci_upper <- mean_speed + 1.96 * std_error
 
  # Display results
  cat("Average Speed Estimate:", mean_speed, "km/day ")
  cat("Average Confidence Interval:", overall_low_CI, "-", overall_high_CI, "km/day ")
  cat(" Rigorous 95% Confidence Interval:", ci_lower, "-", ci_upper, "km/day ")
} else {
  message("No valid speed estimates found in speed_results.")
}

#Plots
library(dplyr)
install.packages("ggplot2")
library(ggplot2)


# Plot speed estimates with confidence intervals
ggplot(speed_results, aes(x = factor(deployment_id), y = speed_est)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), width = 0.2, color = "blue") +
  labs(
    title = "Speed Estimates by Deployment",
    x = "Deployment ID",
    y = "Speed (km/day)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

####END####

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Speed overestimates from camera traps
parts:
Hi Sierra,

It sounds like you have multiple segments from different deer in front of different cameras in a single telemetry object, which makes the model think that the single deer is teleporting around.
If you want to fit one model to a bunch of different deer segments, then you will need to insert large time gaps between the segments, so that a deer could have slowly made its way from one camera to another in that period of time.

Best,
Chris
